name: Sigma Rule Development — Structure, Value Modifiers, Conditions & Examples
command: # Sigma rule structure: title + id + status + logsource + detection + condition
description: Developing Sigma detection rules. Full field reference: title, id (UUID), status (stable/test/experimental/deprecated/unsupported), description, references, author, date, tags (attack.tXXXX), logsource (category+product+service), detection (selection + filter + condition), falsepositives, level (low/medium/high/critical). Value modifiers pipe-chained: field|contains, field|all, field|startswith, field|endswith, field|re. Detection lists (OR logic) vs maps (AND logic). Condition operators: and/or/not, 1/all of them, 1/all of selection*, selection and not 1 of filter_*. Key examples: LSASS 0x1010 access (Sysmon EID 10), NTLM failed logins count >3 per workstation (EID 4776), unusually long PowerShell (EID 4688, regex .{1000,}).
source: CDSA Module 12: YARA & Sigma for SOC Analysts
notes:
=== SIGMA RULE COMPLETE FIELD REFERENCE ===

title: (required)
  → Concise, descriptive rule name
  → Example: "LSASS Access with rare GrantedAccess flag"

id: (recommended)
  → UUID v4 format: xxxxxxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxxxxxxxxxx
  → Uniquely identifies this rule across all SIEMs
  → Example: fa34b441-961a-42fa-a100-ecc28c886725

related: (optional)
  → Links to other rule IDs with relationship type
  → type: derived | similar | obsoletes | merged
  → Example:
    related:
      - id: e98374a6-e2d9-4076-9b5c-11bdb2569995
        type: derived

status: (required)
  → stable        = well-tested, low false positive rate
  → test          = tested but needs more real-world validation
  → experimental  = new rule, may have false positives
  → deprecated    = superseded by another rule
  → unsupported   = not maintained, use with caution

description: (recommended)
  → What the rule detects and why it's suspicious

references: (optional)
  → List of URLs: blog posts, MITRE ATT&CK pages, CVE links

author: (optional)
  → Name/handle of rule creator

date: (optional)
  → Format: YYYY/MM/DD
  → Creation date

modified: (optional)
  → Format: YYYY/MM/DD
  → Last modification date

tags: (optional)
  → MITRE ATT&CK mapping:
    attack.initial_access, attack.execution, attack.persistence,
    attack.privilege_escalation, attack.credential_access,
    attack.lateral_movement, attack.collection, attack.exfiltration,
    attack.command_and_control, attack.defense_evasion, attack.discovery
  → Technique IDs: attack.t1003.001, attack.t1059.001, etc.
  → Other: detection.threat_hunting, cve.2021-XXXXX

level: (recommended)
  → low, medium, high, critical
  → Indicates severity/confidence of alert

falsepositives: (recommended)
  → List of known legitimate scenarios that may trigger rule

logsource: (required)
  → category: process_creation | process_access | network_connection |
               file_event | registry_event | image_load | dns_query
  → product: windows | linux | macos | apache | ...
  → service: security | sysmon | powershell | sshd | ...

  Note: category maps to Sysmon EventIDs via config:
    process_creation   → Sysmon EID 1 or Security EID 4688
    process_access     → Sysmon EID 10
    network_connection → Sysmon EID 3
    image_load         → Sysmon EID 7
    file_event         → Sysmon EID 11
    registry_event     → Sysmon EID 12/13/14

detection: (required)
  → One or more search identifiers (selection/filter/keywords)
  → One condition

=== VALUE MODIFIERS ===
Pipe-appended to field name:

  field|contains: value        → *value* (wildcard both sides)
  field|startswith: value      → value*  (wildcard at end)
  field|endswith: value        → *value  (wildcard at start)
  field|all: [v1, v2]          → field contains v1 AND v2 (list = AND)
  field|contains|all: [v1,v2]  → *v1* AND *v2* (chain modifiers)
  field|re: 'regex_pattern'    → regular expression match

Default (no modifier): exact match (or SIEM-dependent)

Examples:
  Image|endswith: '\\mshta.exe'          → any path ending in \mshta.exe
  CommandLine|contains: 'powershell'     → cmdline contains 'powershell'
  CommandLine|re: '.{1000,}'             → cmdline >= 1000 chars
  TargetImage|endswith: '\\lsass.exe'   → target process is lsass.exe
  ParentImage|startswith: 'C:\\Users\\'  → parent in user profile
  GrantedAccess|endswith: '0x1010'       → access flags ending with 0x1010

=== DETECTION LISTS vs MAPS ===

List (OR logic — any item matches):
  selection:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\\powershell.exe'
      - '\\pwsh.exe'
      - '\\cmd.exe'
  → Matches if Image ends with ANY of the three values

Map (AND logic — all key:value pairs must match):
  selection:
    EventLog: Security
    EventID: 4776
    TargetUserName: '*'
  → Matches only if ALL three conditions are true

Mixed (list of maps → OR of ANDs):
  selection:
    - Image|endswith: '\\example.exe'
    - Description|contains: 'Test executable'
  → Matches if EITHER condition is true

=== CONDITION OPERATORS ===

  condition: selection              → selection must match
  condition: selection1 and selection2   → both must match
  condition: selection1 or selection2    → either must match
  condition: selection and not filter    → selection but exclude filter hits
  condition: 1 of them              → ANY search identifier must match
  condition: all of them            → ALL search identifiers must match
  condition: 1 of selection*        → any identifier starting with 'selection'
  condition: all of selection*      → all identifiers starting with 'selection'
  condition: selection and not 1 of filter_*   → selection minus any filter
  condition: (selection1 or selection2) and selection3  → brackets for order

Aggregation (for counting/thresholds):
  condition: selection | count() > 5
  condition: selection | count(FieldName) by GroupField > 3
  Example: selection2 | count(TargetUserName) by Workstation > 3
    → Alert if count of unique TargetUserName grouped by Workstation > 3

=== EXAMPLE 1: LSASS ACCESS (Sysmon EID 10) ===

  title: LSASS Access with rare GrantedAccess flag
  id: fa34b441-961a-42fa-a100-ecc28c886725
  status: experimental
  description: Detects process access to LSASS with suspicious access flag 0x1010
  date: 2021/11/27
  tags:
    - attack.credential_access
    - attack.t1003.001
  logsource:
    category: process_access
    product: windows
  detection:
    selection:
      TargetImage|endswith: '\\lsass.exe'
      GrantedAccess|endswith: '0x1010'
    condition: selection
  falsepositives:
    - Legitimate security tools
  level: high

Why 0x1010?
  0x0010 = PROCESS_VM_READ
  0x1000 = PROCESS_QUERY_LIMITED_INFORMATION
  Combined = 0x1010 = reading LSASS memory (credential dumping)

Robust version also checks SourceImage path:
  filter_optional_generic_appdata:
    SourceImage|startswith: 'C:\\Users\\'
    SourceImage|contains: '\\AppData\\Local\\'
    GrantedAccess: '0x410'
  condition: selection and not 1 of filter_optional_*

Suspicious GrantedAccess suffixes (credential dumping techniques):
  10, 30, 50, 70, 90, B0, D0, F0, 18, 38, 58, 78, 98, B8, D8, F8,
  1A, 3A, 5A, 7A, 9A, BA, DA, FA, 0x14C2, FF

Suspicious SourceImage paths:
  \\Temp\\, \\Users\\Public\\, \\PerfLogs\\, \\AppData\\, \\htb\\

=== EXAMPLE 2: NTLM FAILED LOGINS COUNT (Security EID 4776) ===

  title: Failed NTLM Logins with Different Accounts from Single Source System
  id: 6309ffc4-8fa2-47cf-96b8-a2f72e58e538
  status: unsupported
  description: Detects suspicious failed logins with different user accounts from single source
  tags:
    - attack.persistence
    - attack.privilege_escalation
    - attack.t1078
  logsource:
    product: windows
    service: security
  detection:
    selection2:
      EventID: 4776
      TargetUserName: '*'
      Workstation: '*'
    condition: selection2 | count(TargetUserName) by Workstation > 3
  falsepositives:
    - Terminal servers
    - Jump servers
    - Citrix farms
  level: medium

EID 4776 = NTLM credential validation event
  → TargetUserName: account being authenticated
  → Workstation: source machine
  → Error code 0xC0000064 = user does not exist (failed login)
  → Count > 3 unique usernames from same workstation = spray indicator

=== EXAMPLE 3: UNUSUALLY LONG POWERSHELL COMMAND (Security EID 4688) ===

  title: Unusually Long PowerShell CommandLine
  id: d0d28567-4b9a-45e2-8bbc-fb1b66a1f7f6
  status: test
  logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
  detection:
    selection:
      EventID: 4688
      NewProcessName|endswith:
        - '\\powershell.exe'
        - '\\pwsh.exe'
        - '\\cmd.exe'
    selection_powershell:
      CommandLine|contains:
        - 'powershell.exe'
        - 'pwsh.exe'
    selection_length:
      CommandLine|re: '.{1000,}'
    condition: selection and selection_powershell and selection_length
  level: low

Pattern: attackers use base64+gzip compressed payloads → very long cmdlines
Common evasion: cmd.exe /b /c start /b /min powershell.exe -nop -w hidden ...
